root_cause.text: The SCX_KICK_WAIT implementation performed a busy-wait in hardirq context inside kick_cpus_irq_workfn(), which prevented the waiting CPU from rescheduling or advancing its own kick_sync, enabling cyclic dependencies between CPUs to cause a deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "the irq_work runs in hardirq context, the waiting CPU cannot reschedule and its own kick_sync never advances. If multiple CPUs form a wait cycle, all CPUs deadlock." The patch replaces the hardirq busy-wait (smp_cond_load_acquire) with a balance callback that drops the rq lock and enables IRQs, allowing the CPU to process IPIs and advance its kick_sync while waiting.

vuln_statements.explanation: This busy-wait loop in hardirq context prevents the waiting CPU from making progress, leading to deadlock when cyclic dependencies exist. The waiting CPU cannot reschedule or advance its own kick_sync, causing indefinite wait.

This initializes the IRQ work as HARD, causing the entire kick_cpus_irq_workfn (including the busy-wait) to execute in hardirq context, which prevents the waiting CPU from rescheduling and is core to the vulnerability.

This loop iterates over all CPUs to wait on, all within hardirq context. If the set includes CPUs that are part of a cyclic dependency, each will busy-wait without progress, exacerbating the deadlock.
This line sets the flag that enables the busy-wait loop. Without it, the loop would be skipped. It directly controls whether the busy-wait occurs and is therefore critical to triggering the deadlock.

This line captures the kick_sync value that the busy-wait will compare against. If the captured value is stale or the expected update cannot happen (due to hardirq context), the wait will never terminate.

This guard allows early exit only if should_wait is false, but when true it falls through to the busy-wait loop. It directly controls whether the busy-wait occurs and is therefore a key enabler of the vulnerability.

This line in schedule() is the expected release that waiting CPUs rely on to advance their sync value. If this update cannot execute due to the waiting CPU being stuck in hardirq busy-wait, the wait persists indefinitely, completing the deadlock cycle.

This condition determines which CPUs are waited on. If a CPU is included but cannot progress (e.g., it is part of a cyclic dependency), deadlock occurs. The mask selection is essential to the waiting logic.
This allocation creates the 'cpus_to_wait' mask that stores the set of CPUs to wait on. The existence of this mask enables the waiting mechanism used in the vulnerable busy-wait loop.
This declaration defines the per-rq field that stores the set of CPUs to wait on. It is essential for the waiting logic and its presence enables the vulnerable behavior.

This declaration defines the per-rq field that the busy-wait uses as the synchronization variable. Stale or unsynchronized updates (due to hardirq context preventing rescheduling) contribute to the deadlock condition.
